title: Differentiation between delirium and dementia through spontaneous speech
summary: The goal of DEESA is to analyze language in individuals with delirium and dementia. For this purpose, geriatric patients are asked to complete various tasks during and after their stay in a medical facility, which are designed to elicit spontaneous speech. The conversation between the study staff and participants is recorded and automatically processed. Using the collected dataset, machine learning models are trained to enable differentiation between delirium and dementia. DEESA is a cooperation project between Prof. Dr.-Ing. Tanja Schultz (Universität Bremen) and Prof. Dr. med. Tania Zieschang (Universitätsmedizin Oldenburg) within the scope of the research training group HEARAZ.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- patients receiving treatment at the University Hospital for Geriatrics at Klinikum Oldenburg or the Geriatric Clinic at Rehazentrum Oldenburg.
- geriatric patients  ≥ 70 years with multimorbidity, or ≥ 80 years (regardless of multimorbidity).
- suspected or confirmed diagnosis of dementia or delirium (delirium/dementia group).
- no neurocognitive impairment (control group)
Exclusion criteria:
- critical illness (clinical staff determines whether participation poses a risk to the patient)
- acute or corrected sensory impairment affecting current speech comprehension
- acute or persistent (historical) speech/language disorder affecting current speech production (e.g., aphasia)
- currently predominant psychiatric condition (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, severe depressive symptoms)
